reason: I'll start with the arteries: the picture shows where the lining fits inside their strong, elastic wall.
expectation: I expect to make a lined artery that can stretch and spring back as blood flows.

alternatives.reason: The capillaries and body cells also have a clear purpose, but I'll build the outward route first.

effect: The lined arterial vessels complete the outward-route goal; next I'll work on exchange near body cells.
reaction: The arrows away from the heart make the artery's role clear.
reason: The thin capillary walls and nearby cells suggest a place for oxygen and food to move to cells.
expectation: I expect capillaries positioned near body cells to form an exchange area, though I'm not sure how the game will show it.

alternatives.reason: The vein lining also fits the return-route goal, but I want to build the exchange area first.

effect: The capillary bed shows oxygen and nutrients moving to cells and carbon dioxide moving toward blood. I'll build the return route next.
reaction: It's useful to see that blood cells stay inside while dissolved materials cross.
reason: The venous wall needs a lining before it can become the return route with valves.
expectation: I expect a lined vein, possibly still needing its one-way valve flaps.

alternatives.reason: Connecting arteries to the capillary bed also makes sense, but I want to prepare the vein first.

effect: The veins now have a smooth lining and point toward the heart; they still need valves for the return-route goal.
reaction: The opposite arrow directions make veins easy to distinguish from arteries.
reason: I'll add the valve flaps to complete the return route.
expectation: I expect veins with valves that open for blood moving toward the heart and close against backward flow.

alternatives.reason: The arteries and capillaries also need connecting, but I'll finish preparing the veins first.

effect: The valves complete the return route, and the new goal is to join all three vessel routes.
reaction: Seeing a contracting muscle help push blood past the valves is useful.
reason: I'll connect the arteries to the capillary bed first, following blood outward from the heart.
expectation: I expect a connected route from arteries into the exchange vessels, still needing the venous return.

alternatives.reason: Connecting capillaries to veins also fits the goal, but I prefer to follow the route outward first.

effect: The arteries now connect to the capillaries, leaving open ends for the return route.
reaction: The branching makes the outward route easy to follow.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should join the return route to the exchange bed.
expectation: I expect a connected path from arteries through capillaries and back through veins.

effect: The completed network joins arteries, capillaries and veins into a route away from and back toward the heart. All chapter goals are complete.
reaction: Seeing the whole route connected was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the capillary bed was most worthwhile: it showed what crosses between blood and body cells, and what stays inside the vessels.

leastWorthwhile.text: Lining the artery and vein felt a little repetitive, though their opposite arrow directions helped distinguish their jobs.

surprise.text: I didn't expect the picture to show a contracting muscle helping push blood through the vein valves.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals gave the pairings a clear purpose. The final combination was the only offered action.

continue.text: I might continue: connecting the routes was satisfying, and I'd be curious to see how the heart fits into the network, though some assembly steps felt predictable.
